route: source-data id-level match (S1 XLSX) + paper Table 2 explicit IS<k>(Q<n>) labels; CFA loadings vs Table 3 as corroboration

Q-code -> wording is the paper's own explicit Table 2 label 'IS1(Q20)'..'IS5(Q24)'. One-factor CFA loadings 0.904/0.875/0.893/0.896/0.892 vs published Table 3 0.903/0.877/0.890/0.897/0.892 corroborate but are too tightly bunched (0.877-0.903) to separate items alone. Does NOT establish: that the paper's Table 2 printed the right wording beside each Q code (taken on the paper's explicit label), nor that the English matches the administered Chinese.

route: id-level agreement with S1 source columns (explicit Q-code labels in Table 2) + CFA loadings vs Table 3

Route B (corroboration): one-factor CFA standardized loadings 0.903/0.890/0.900/0.913/0.906 vs Table 3 0.906/0.894/0.900/0.917/0.906. route: explicit code labels (paper Table 2 RAk(Qn)) + id-level match of live items to S1 columns + Table 3 loadings
evidence: Route A (code -> S1 column, decisive): each live RA<k> agrees with S1 column Q<9+k> id-for-id on 207/207 respondents (RA1=Q10, RA2=Q11, RA3=Q12, RA4=Q13, RA5=Q14), and no other of the 35 columns Q5..Q39 reaches full agreement for any item (best other: RA1 Q12 112/207; RA2 Q13 81/207; RA3 Q10 112/207; RA4 Q10 85/207; RA5 Q10 70/207), so every item is distinguished from every other. This also rules out the positional reading of S1's permuted physical order Q10,Q11,Q14,Q12,Q13.
